parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write an equation to show the reaction for the standard enthalpy change of formation of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Water is one of the products in the reaction of $\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{NH}_3$, as shown in reaction 2.

$$\text{reaction 2} \qquad \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NH}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{BN} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Table 3.1 shows information about the standard enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, of some substances.

Table 3.1

| substance | $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}/\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$ | $-1264$ |
| $\text{NH}_3$ | $-46$ |
| $\text{BN}$ | $-134$ |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | $-286$ |

Calculate the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, for reaction 2 using the data from Table 3.1.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Boron carbide is a hard crystalline solid that has a melting point greater than $2000^{\circ}\text{C}$.
parts.text: Suggest the structure and bonding in boron carbide.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
$100\text{ g}$ of pure boron carbide contains $78.26\text{ g}$ of boron.

Calculate the empirical formula of boron carbide.

Show your working.
